rationale: The route (MESSAGE→CONVERSATION→CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→USER) is correctly used to select messages whose channel has a Kenji Sato membership row, matching the prompt's plain-language request. Kenji's five channel memberships (project-alpha-dev, core-infra, model-research, product-growth, frontend) are all present in channel_members, and his non-membership in #engineering and the agent-Sophie DM is also confirmed by the base seed. The two match roles (Łukasz's and Priya's circuit-tracer OOM fix messages in #project-alpha-dev) are planned additions to an already-membership-qualified channel, which is permitted at design stage. The negatives cover distinct, well-motivated failure modes: correct topic/wrong channel (#engineering messages, including one authored by Kenji himself to test authorship vs. membership), correct topic/wrong conversation type (DM), and correct channel/wrong topic (#model-research off-topic message). Cross-checking the base seed confirms no accidental extra matches exist among Kenji's channels (C_INFRA and C_MODEL discussions concern unrelated OOM/model topics, not circuit-tracer). The access plan (conversations.members or users.conversations, then conversations.history) is realistic and uses only documented APIs. Written attributes (message_text, channel_id, user_id) are bare columns. The design is concise, plausible, and the negatives meaningfully probe the membership-vs-authorship and topic-vs-scope distinctions without leaking the answer.
